```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

import re
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Color palette matching site theme
COLORS = {
    'primary': '#5A317E',
    'muted': '#CFC9BA',
    'text': '#2C3A2F',
}

# --- Conversation topics, as each helpline records them -------------------
# The paper's published figure source data (zenodo.7090520). Sheets S3 and S4
# hold the two helplines' own topic taxonomies rather than a harmonised set:
# S3 is Nummer gegen Kummer (its youth line dominates the under-20 sample,
# its parent line the 20+ one), S4 is TelefonSeelsorge, whose 20+ sample is
# an order of magnitude larger than anyone else's.
_COLS = {"Category": "category", "Topic": "topictitle", "Week": "wdate",
         "Observations": "Number of observations", "Age group": "agegroup"}
_s3 = pd.read_excel("data/SI_Data.xlsx", sheet_name="Fig S3").rename(columns=_COLS)
_s4 = pd.read_excel("data/SI_Data.xlsx", sheet_name="Fig S4").rename(columns=_COLS)
for _d in (_s3, _s4):
    _d["agegroup"] = _d["agegroup"].astype(str).str.strip()

# S3 lists nine category totals alongside the sub-topics they aggregate, under
# the category's own name; plotting both would draw each conversation twice.
# Drop the totals and keep the category as hover context instead.
CATEGORY_NAMES = {
    "add": "Addiction/self-harm", "fam": "Problems in family",
    "livsit": "Living situation", "love": "Relationship/love",
    "peer": "Friends/peer group", "psysoc": "Psycho-social/health",
    "school": "School/education", "sex": "Sexuality", "viol": "Violence, abuse",
}
_s3 = _s3[~_s3.topictitle.isin(CATEGORY_NAMES.values())].copy()
_s3["group"] = _s3.category.map(CATEGORY_NAMES)


# Plotly writes datetimes as 31-character ISO strings, once per point per
# series; with a few hundred series that dominates the page. Plain dates cost
# a third of that, and float32 halves the binary payload for the values.
def _dates(col):
    return col.dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def _vals(col):
    return col.round(2).astype("float32")


def create_spaghetti_plot(data, default_topic, group_col=None):
    """Spaghetti plot of every topic, one highlighted, the rest as context."""
    fig = go.Figure()

    for topic, d in data.groupby("topictitle", sort=True):
        d = d.sort_values("wdate")
        name = str(topic).strip()
        is_default = name == default_topic
        group = d[group_col].iloc[0] if group_col else None

        # 217 series across the three tabs, so keep the payload lean: no
        # per-point customdata, and coefficients rounded to what is displayed.
        tail = f"<br><i>{group}</i>" if group else ""

        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_dates(d["wdate"]), y=_vals(d["Coefficient"]),
            name=name, mode="lines",
            line=dict(color=COLORS['primary'] if is_default else COLORS['muted'],
                      width=2.5 if is_default else 1.2),
            opacity=1.0 if is_default else 0.4,
            showlegend=False,   # far too many series for a legend
            hovertemplate=(f"<b>{name}</b><br>%{{x|%b %d, %Y}}<br>"
                           "Deviation: %{y:.2f} p.p." + tail +
                           "<extra></extra>"),
            meta=dict(topic=name)))

    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dash", line_color="rgba(44,58,47,0.25)",
                  line_width=1)

    # Standing label for whichever line is highlighted; the click handler
    # rewrites it.
    fig.add_annotation(
        name="highlight-label",
        x=0, y=1.06, xref="paper", yref="paper", xanchor="left",
        yanchor="bottom", text=default_topic, showarrow=False,
        font=dict(size=12, color=COLORS['primary']))

    fig.update_layout(
        template="plotly_white",
        paper_bgcolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)', plot_bgcolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)',
        font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", color=COLORS['text'],
                  size=11),
        showlegend=False, hovermode='closest',
        height=430, margin=dict(l=64, r=24, t=42, b=54),
        yaxis=dict(title="Deviation from baseline (p.p.)", showgrid=True,
                   gridcolor='rgba(44,58,47,0.07)', zeroline=False),
        xaxis=dict(showgrid=True, gridcolor='rgba(44,58,47,0.07)'))

    return fig


spaghetti_ts = create_spaghetti_plot(
    _s4[_s4.agegroup == "Age > 19"], "Loneliness/isolation")
spaghetti_ngk_young = create_spaghetti_plot(
    _s3[_s3.agegroup == "Age < 20"], "Boredom", group_col="group")
spaghetti_ngk_adult = create_spaghetti_plot(
    _s3[_s3.agegroup == "Age > 19"], "Mental health prob.", group_col="group")
```

```{python}
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

# --- Both US helplines, state by state ----------------------------------
# Panel b of Fig. 4 and of Extended Data Fig. 6: each state's weekly calls
# as a deviation from its own time-averaged mean, so states of very
# different size sit on one scale. Two panels, because the two helplines
# differ by an order of magnitude in how far they swing.

US_STATE_PANELS = [
    ("National Suicide Prevention Lifeline",
     "data/nature_fig4_lifeline_us.xlsx", "Panels b-e"),
    ("Disaster Distress Helpline",
     "data/nature_edfig6_disaster_distress.xlsx", "Panel b"),
]

us_states_fig = make_subplots(
    rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.12,
    subplot_titles=[t for t, _p, _s in US_STATE_PANELS])

for _row, (_title, _path, _sheet) in enumerate(US_STATE_PANELS, start=1):
    _st = pd.read_excel(_path, sheet_name=_sheet).rename(columns={
        "State/province name": "state",
        "Residual (log deviation)": "resid",
        "Residual (log deviation), US average": "usavg"})

    for _state, _g in _st.groupby("state"):
        _g = _g.sort_values("wdate")
        us_states_fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=_dates(_g.wdate), y=_vals(_g.resid), name=_state, mode="lines",
            line=dict(color=COLORS['muted'], width=1), opacity=0.45,
            showlegend=False,
            customdata=[f"{v:+.1f}" for v in _g.resid],
            hovertemplate=(f"<b>{_state}</b><br>%{{x|%b %d, %Y}}<br>"
                           "Deviation: %{customdata} log points<extra></extra>")),
            row=_row, col=1)

    # National average drawn last so it sits on top of the state lines
    _nat = _st.drop_duplicates("wdate").sort_values("wdate")
    us_states_fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=_dates(_nat.wdate), y=_vals(_nat.usavg),
        name="United States average", mode="lines",
        line=dict(color=COLORS['primary'], width=2.5), opacity=1.0,
        showlegend=False,
        customdata=[f"{v:+.1f}" for v in _nat.usavg],
        hovertemplate=("<b>United States average</b><br>%{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>"
                       "Deviation: %{customdata} log points<extra></extra>")),
        row=_row, col=1)

    us_states_fig.add_hline(y=0, line_dash="dash", line_width=1,
                            line_color="rgba(44,58,47,0.25)", row=_row, col=1)
    us_states_fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Deviation (log points)",
                               showgrid=True, gridcolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.07)",
                               zeroline=False, row=_row, col=1)

# Standing label for whichever state is highlighted; the click handler finds
# it by name and rewrites it.
us_states_fig.add_annotation(
    name="highlight-label",
    x=1, y=1.06, xref="paper", yref="paper", xanchor="right", yanchor="bottom",
    text="United States average", showarrow=False,
    font=dict(size=12, color=COLORS['primary']))

us_states_fig.update_xaxes(showgrid=True, gridcolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.07)",
                           zeroline=False)
us_states_fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", color=COLORS['text'], size=11),
    showlegend=False,
    hovermode="closest",
    height=560, margin=dict(l=66, r=24, t=44, b=48),
    hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="#FCFAF4", bordercolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.5)",
                    font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=11,
                              color=COLORS['text'])),
)
for _a in us_states_fig.layout.annotations[:2]:
    _a.font.size = 12
    _a.xanchor = "left"
    _a.x = 0
```

```{python}
import numpy as np

# --- Map of social-revolutionary terror groups, 1860-1950 ---------------
# Replication data from Klotzbuecher, Krieger & Meierrieks (2021).

PLATE = "#FCFAF4"        # chart surface; the palette below is validated on it
LAND = "#F1ECDE"

# All six ideologies are kept, but only two carry saturated colour: an
# all-pairs colour-vision check caps a map at four categorical hues, and the
# paper is about social-revolutionary terror. So anarchist and leftist are
# emphasised in mauve and crimson, while the other four recede to a
# single-hue neutral ramp separated by lightness. Hover names each exactly.
MAP_SERIES = [
    ("Anarchist", "#7040A0", 10, 1.0),
    ("Leftist", "#B3324A", 10, 1.0),
    ("Nationalist", "#5F5A4E", 7, 0.75),
    ("Rightist", "#7C7768", 7, 0.75),
    ("Religious", "#999280", 7, 0.75),
    ("Other", "#B0A996", 7, 0.75),
]
MAP_GROUPING = {k: k for k, _c, _s, _o in MAP_SERIES}

groups = pd.read_stata("data/old_terror.dta")
groups = groups[(groups.StrYear <= 1950)
                & groups["_ycity"].notna()
                & groups["_xcity"].notna()].copy()
groups["series"] = groups["Ideology"].astype(str).map(MAP_GROUPING)
groups["lat"] = groups["_ycity"].astype(float)
groups["lon"] = groups["_xcity"].astype(float)

# Groups sharing a city sit on identical coordinates; fan them out on a small
# spiral so each one stays visible and hoverable.
for (la, lo), idx in groups.groupby(["_ycity", "_xcity"]).groups.items():
    if len(idx) < 2:
        continue
    for k, i in enumerate(idx):
        ring, pos = divmod(k, 8)
        r = 0.55 + 0.5 * ring
        ang = 2 * np.pi * pos / min(len(idx), 8) + ring * 0.4
        groups.loc[i, "lat"] = la + r * np.sin(ang)
        groups.loc[i, "lon"] = lo + r * np.cos(ang) / max(np.cos(np.radians(la)), 0.35)

def _span(r):
    if r.endunknown == 1 or pd.isna(r.EndYear):
        return f"{int(r.StrYear)}–"
    return f"{int(r.StrYear)}–{int(r.EndYear)}"

groups["span"] = groups.apply(_span, axis=1)
groups["place"] = groups.apply(
    lambda r: f"{r.City}, {r.Country}".replace("*", "")
    if str(r.City).strip() not in ("", ".") else str(r.Country), axis=1)

terror_map = go.Figure()
# Context categories first so the emphasised ones draw on top of them
for _name, _color, _size, _opacity in sorted(MAP_SERIES, key=lambda s: s[3]):
    d = groups[groups.series == _name]
    terror_map.add_trace(go.Scattergeo(
        lat=d.lat, lon=d.lon, name=f"{_name} ({len(d)})",
        mode="markers",
        marker=dict(size=_size, color=_color, opacity=_opacity,
                    line=dict(width=1.4, color=PLATE)),
        customdata=np.stack([d.Group, d.place, d.Ideology.astype(str), d.span], axis=-1),
        hovertemplate=("<b>%{customdata[0]}</b><br>%{customdata[1]}<br>"
                       "%{customdata[2]} · %{customdata[3]}<extra></extra>"),
    ))

terror_map.update_geos(
    projection_type="natural earth",
    showland=True, landcolor=LAND,
    showocean=True, oceancolor=PLATE,
    showlakes=False,
    showcountries=True, countrycolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.28)",
    coastlinecolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.45)", coastlinewidth=0.6,
    showframe=True, framecolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.35)", framewidth=1,
    lataxis_range=[-40, 66], lonaxis_range=[-126, 146],
    bgcolor=PLATE,
)
terror_map.update_layout(
    paper_bgcolor=PLATE, plot_bgcolor=PLATE,
    font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", color=COLORS['text'], size=11),
    margin=dict(l=4, r=4, t=4, b=34),
    height=560,
    hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor=PLATE, bordercolor="rgba(44,58,47,0.5)",
                    font=dict(family="IBM Plex Mono, monospace", size=11,
                              color=COLORS['text'])),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=0.02, xanchor="center", x=0.5,
                bgcolor="rgba(252,250,244,0.85)", borderwidth=0,
                font=dict(size=10)),
    dragmode="pan",
)
```

:::

Deviation of conversation topics from their 2019 baseline, in percentage
points, for calls to Germany's two nationwide helplines for young people.
Each tab uses that helpline's **own** topic taxonomy rather than a harmonised
one, so the categories differ between them: **TelefonSeelsorge**, the
country's largest helpline, records 41 topics for its adult callers, while
**Nummer gegen Kummer** records 88 finer-grained ones, split here into its
youth line (callers under 20) and its parent line (callers 20 and over).

Hover any line for the topic, the deviation that week and, for Nummer gegen
Kummer, the broader category it belongs to; click a line to highlight it and
name it above the plot. Based on some three million calls between January
2019 and May 2022.

:::

::: {#us-states-figure .callout-note collapse="true" title="Interactive Figure: US Helpline Calls by State"}

Each grey line is one US state; the mauve line is the nationwide weekly average.
Calls are shown as deviations from each state's own average over the period, so
states of very different size can share one scale, and the two helplines get
their own panel because they swing by very different amounts. Hover any line to
identify the state, or click it to highlight that state in **both** panels and
name it above the plot. Source data for Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 6,
covering January 2020 to March 2021.

:::

```{=html}
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const PRIMARY = '#5A317E';
  const MUTED = '#CFC9BA';

  // There is no legend on these plots (~20 topics would make an unusable
  // one); clicking a line highlights it and names it in the corner label.
  function setupPlotClickHandlers(plotDiv) {
    if (!plotDiv || !plotDiv.data || typeof plotDiv.on !== 'function') return;

    // initPlots runs several times, and Plotly drops its listeners whenever it
    // redraws a plot, so rebind every pass and clear first to avoid stacking
    // duplicate handlers. A "already bound" flag cannot be trusted: it would
    // survive a redraw that silently removed the handler.
    if (typeof plotDiv.removeAllListeners === 'function') {
      plotDiv.removeAllListeners('plotly_click');
    }

    const numTraces = plotDiv.data.length;

    function highlight(clickedIndex) {
      // Match on the series name, not the index: the state figure repeats the
      // same state in both panels, and clicking one should light up both.
      const picked = plotDiv.data[clickedIndex];
      if (!picked) return;
      const target = picked.name;

      const updates = {
        'line.color': [],
        'line.width': [],
        'opacity': []
      };

      for (let i = 0; i < numTraces; i++) {
        if (plotDiv.data[i].name === target) {
          updates['line.color'].push(PRIMARY);
          updates['line.width'].push(2.5);
          updates['opacity'].push(1.0);
        } else {
          updates['line.color'].push(MUTED);
          updates['line.width'].push(1.2);
          updates['opacity'].push(0.4);
        }
      }

      Plotly.restyle(plotDiv, updates);

      const anns = (plotDiv.layout && plotDiv.layout.annotations) || [];
      const slot = anns.findIndex(function(a) { return a.name === 'highlight-label'; });
      if (slot >= 0 && target) {
        const patch = {};
        patch['annotations[' + slot + '].text'] = target;
        Plotly.relayout(plotDiv, patch);
      }
    }

    plotDiv.on('plotly_click', function(data) {
      if (!data.points || data.points.length === 0) return;
      highlight(data.points[0].curveNumber);
    });
  }

  // Attach handlers only to the two spaghetti figures, so the map and the
  // call-volume chart keep their own behaviour.
  const SPAGHETTI = ['#helpline-figure', '#us-states-figure'];

  function initPlots() {
    SPAGHETTI.forEach(function(sel) {
      document.querySelectorAll(sel + ' .js-plotly-plot').forEach(function(plot) {
        if (plot.data) {
          setupPlotClickHandlers(plot);
        }
      });
    });
  }

  // Try immediately and also after a delay (for tab switching)
  setTimeout(initPlots, 500);
  setTimeout(initPlots, 1500);

  // Re-init when tabs are clicked
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-link').forEach(function(tab) {
    tab.addEventListener('click', function() {
      setTimeout(initPlots, 300);
    });
  });

  // Plots rendered inside the collapsed callout (or hidden tabs) have zero
  // width; resize them whenever a collapse or tab is shown
  function resizePlots() {
    if (!window.Plotly) return;
    document.querySelectorAll('.js-plotly-plot').forEach(function(p) {
      Plotly.Plots.resize(p);
    });
  }
  // The map keeps a fixed aspect ratio, so a fixed pixel height leaves dead
  // space on narrow screens; size it from its own width instead.
  function sizeMap() {
    const map = document.querySelector('#terror-map-figure .js-plotly-plot');
    if (!map || !window.Plotly) return;
    // Measure the holder, not the plot: the plot's own width may be stale.
    const holder = map.parentElement;
    const w = Math.floor((holder ? holder.clientWidth : map.clientWidth) || 0);
    if (!w) return;
    const h = Math.max(300, Math.min(560, Math.round(w / 1.75)));
    const fl = map._fullLayout || {};
    if (Math.abs((fl.width || 0) - w) > 4 || Math.abs((fl.height || 0) - h) > 4) {
      Plotly.relayout(map, {width: w, height: h});
    }
    // Quarto stamps the figure height inline on the div; clear it too or the
    // container keeps reserving the original height.
    map.style.height = h + 'px';
  }

  // The two-panel state figure is legible at desktop width but cramped on a
  // phone; pull in the margins and type rather than letting labels clip.
  function sizeUsFig() {
    const g = document.querySelector('#us-states-figure .js-plotly-plot');
    if (!g || !window.Plotly) return;
    const w = Math.floor((g.parentElement ? g.parentElement.clientWidth
                                          : g.clientWidth) || 0);
    if (!w) return;
    const narrow = w < 520;
    const yTitle = narrow ? 'Log points' : 'Deviation (log points)';
    Plotly.relayout(g, {
      width: w,
      height: narrow ? 460 : 560,
      'margin.l': narrow ? 48 : 66,
      'margin.r': narrow ? 10 : 24,
      'font.size': narrow ? 9 : 11,
      'yaxis.title.text': yTitle,
      'yaxis2.title.text': yTitle,
      'xaxis2.nticks': narrow ? 4 : 9,
      // 0 and 1 are the panel titles, 2 is the highlight label
      'annotations[0].font.size': narrow ? 10 : 12,
      'annotations[1].font.size': narrow ? 10 : 12,
      'annotations[2].font.size': narrow ? 10 : 12
    });
    g.style.height = (narrow ? 460 : 560) + 'px';
  }

  document.addEventListener('shown.bs.collapse', function() {
    setTimeout(resizePlots, 50);
    setTimeout(sizeMap, 60);
    setTimeout(sizeUsFig, 60);
    // Plotly may still be initialising the plot that just became visible
    [300, 900, 1800].forEach(function(t) { setTimeout(initPlots, t); });
  });
  document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', function() {
    setTimeout(resizePlots, 50);
  });

  let figResizeTimer;
  window.addEventListener('resize', function() {
    clearTimeout(figResizeTimer);
    figResizeTimer = setTimeout(function() { sizeMap(); sizeUsFig(); }, 150);
  });
  [600, 1600].forEach(function(t) {
    setTimeout(function() { sizeMap(); sizeUsFig(); }, t);
  });
});
</script>
```

* "Young people's mental and social distress in times of international crisis: evidence from helpline calls, 2019-2022", with M. Br&uuml;lhart and R. Lalive. [*Scientific Reports*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-39064-y) 13, 11858 (2023).
  [Stata code](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7090520) | [PNAS News Feature](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2214564119)

* "Mental health concerns during the COVID-19 pandemic as revealed by helpline calls", with M. Br&uuml;lhart, R. Lalive and S. Reich. [*Nature*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-04099-6) 600: 121-126 (2021).
  [PDF](https://rdcu.be/cEdwR) | [Stata code](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5495829) | [Behind the paper](https://communities.springernature.com/posts/mental-health-concerns-during-the-pandemic-as-revealed-by-helpline-calls) | [Coronapod](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-021-03649-2) | [Nature News&Views](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-021-03038-9)

* "Lost in Lockdown? COVID-19, Social Distancing, and Mental Health in Germany", with S. Reich. *Covid Economics* 22: 117-153 (2020)


### Political economy

::: {#terror-map-figure .callout-note collapse="true" title="Interactive Figure: Terror Groups, 1860-1950"}

```{python}
#| echo: false
terror_map.show(config={
    "responsive": True,
    "displayModeBar": True, "displaylogo": False,
    # Drag pans, the buttons zoom. Scroll zoom stays off so that scrolling
    # past the map does not hijack the page.
    "scrollZoom": False,
    "modeBarButtons": [["zoomInGeo", "zoomOutGeo", "resetGeo"]],
})
```

Each marker is one terror group, placed at the city where it formed; hover for
its name, ideology and years of activity. The two social-revolutionary
ideologies the paper is about &mdash; anarchist and leftist &mdash; are drawn in
colour; the remaining ideologies recede into greys but are all still shown and
named on hover. Drag to pan and use the buttons at the top right to zoom
&mdash; useful for the dense European cluster. Groups from the same city are
fanned out slightly so they stay distinguishable, and present-day borders are
drawn for orientation only.

Group data are from J. Tschantret, ["The old terrorism: a dataset,
1860&ndash;1969"](https://doi.org/10.1080/03050629.2019.1649259), *International
Interactions* 45(5): 933&ndash;948 (2019), as used in "Class warfare" below.

:::

* "Chapter 20: Tourism", with G. Schulze. In [*The Cambridge Handbook on the Economics of Terrorism*](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/cambridge-handbook-on-the-economics-of-terrorism/15D5BA8B0089979A45B2D0196741E16A) (eds. Basuchoudary & Schulze): 442-456 (2026)

* "Class warfare: Political exclusion of the poor and the roots of social-revolutionary terrorism, 1860-1950", with T. Krieger and D. Meierrieks. [*Defence and Peace Economics*](https://doi.org/10.1080/10242694.2021.1940456) 32(6): 681-697 (2021). Also in: *On Terrorist Groups* (Routledge, 2023).
